thread:
oncall-bot: HIGH PAGER — multiple 5xx + p50/p95 latency spike observed in eu-central1 routing layer (incident id: RTE-2026-0423). Paging routing-oncall.

sanjay: acked — jumping in. @katie are you still routing-oncall?

katie: yup oncall here. seeing elevated queue depth on eu frontends and a bunch of fallback model selections. digging in now. starting with request traces and routing config.

lee: quick snapshot from the frontends (12:23:09 - 12:26:12 UTC):
```
[12:23:10] queue_depth=312 route=eu-central1 shard=frontend-12 req_id=tx-9b3f status=queued
[12:23:12] route_decision: fallback_to_model=redwood-lite-v1 weight=0.65 reason=policy-tier-unavailable
[12:23:13] model_connect_err: upstream_timeout host=dedicated-eu-01
[12:25:03] p95_latency=2.9s p50=430ms errors_5xx=118
```

maria: customer-impact quick note: vendor-corp-prod and medsys-inc had ~420 failed requests total in that interval (mostly timeouts). Customer alerts firing. Escalating to account execs.

ash: preliminary hypothesis: new routing policy commit (routing-policy: feature/weighted-fallback) deployed at 12:22 UTC changed fallback_weight semantics — instead of decreasing preference for lower-tier models it accidentally increased weight on fallback path when regional capacity is low. Could cause spillover to fallback models and then to dev-tier when capacity still constrained. Pulling the policy diff now.

ash: diff snippet from policy repo:
```
- fallback_weight: 0.3  # prefer primary
+ fallback_weight: 0.7  # prefer fallback when region capacity < 30%
```
This looks inverted relative to previous intent. Maybe a typo in operator ordering.

jordan: I can confirm the deploy was a partial rollout (canary across eu frontends) at 12:22:18. Canary traffic was 10% initially, then auto-escalated to 40% due to autoscale script thinking latency ok.

katie: action: pausing canary and rolling back routing-policy to previous commit. @ops-bot can you run the rollback play?

ops-bot: runbook step: rolling back routing-policy canary -> target commit routing-policy@9f2a1b. Executing…

ops-bot: rollback started (12:27:05 UTC). Canary traffic set to 0%.

oncall-bot: METRIC UPDATE — 12:30 UTC: p95 latency down from 2.9s to 620ms; 5xx rate down 75%. Continuing to monitor.

lee: after rollback we still saw a handful of misroutes (12:31–12:34) where requests that had been preferring redwood-lite ended up hitting dev-tier proxies and returned 502. Here's a routing decision trace excerpt (sanitized):
```
{"req_id":"tx-9b3f","region":"eu-central1","policy_version":"9f2a1b","chosen_model":"dev-mini-v0","decision_path":["primary","fallback","dev-tier"],"reasons":["capacity_threshold","fallback_weight_eval"]}
```

sanjay: that decision_path shows a cascade: primary unavailable -> fallback selected -> fallback couldn't attach to dedicated pool -> dev-tier selected. Need logs from model-proxy side for the dev-tier 502s. @lee can you grab proxy logs for proxies dev-proxy-3 and dev-proxy-4?

lee: grabbing now. snippets:
```
[12:23:14] proxy dev-proxy-3: attach_err: pool_exhausted
[12:23:15] proxy dev-proxy-4: return_code=502 upstream_closed
[12:32:10] proxy dev-proxy-3: attach_ok
```

maria: customer-impact addendum for postmortem: affected customers had increased tail latency and ~10% error ratio for short period (~8m). No data loss; retries recovered many requests. Will compile SLAs impacted and list of customer IDs for comms.

ash: hypothesis refinement: bug is twofold — (1) fallback_weight inversion in new policy made fallback path more attractive than intended, and (2) the autoscaler for dedicated-eu pool misreported healthy capacity after brief transient, causing fallback selection to cascade. The misreport allowed canary percentage to ramp and then cascade into dev-tier when fallback could not get attachments.

katie: intermediate mitigation done: rollback complete at 12:27:05, we throttled canary ramping and added a temporary hard cap to fallback_weight in runtime config: `fallback_weight_max=0.4`. Monitoring.

jordan: confirm metrics: at 12:35 UTC request error budget spike contained. No further pager escalations.

oncall-bot: NOTE — please preserve the traces with tag "RTE-2026-0423" and upload logs to the incident artifacts bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/RTE-2026-0423/ (trace IDs: tx-9b3f, tx-9b4a, tx-9c01).

sanjay: next steps for RCA doc:
- collect routing-policy diff and deploy timestamps (owner: ash)
- export autoscaler metrics and dedicated-eu pool attach logs (owner: lee)
- collect proxy 502 traces and model attach rejection counts (owner: katie)
- customer impact & comms draft (owner: maria)
- timeline & hypothesis writeup (owner: sanjay)

katie: I'll pull the model attach rejection histogram and paste into incident artifacts. Also will include the runtime config change that applied the `fallback_weight_max` override.

lee: timeline draft (short):
- 12:22:18 UTC — routing-policy canary roll started (feature/weighted-fallback)
- 12:23:05 UTC — frontends queue depth increases; model attach failures begin
- 12:25:00 UTC — oncall alerts triggered (p95 and 5xx)
- 12:26:00 UTC — autoscaler for dedicated-eu temporarily scales down due to probe flapping (suspected)
- 12:27:05 UTC — rollback to routing-policy@9f2a1b executed; canary paused
- 12:30:00 UTC — metrics improving; throttles and fallback_weight_max applied
- 12:35:00 UTC — incident contained, no active pager

maria: saving that timeline to incident doc. Will ping account managers for affected customers with ETA and summary.

ash: for the RCA I'll repo the exact policy tests that would have caught the inversion (unit test for weight semantics + simulated load test against autoscaler flapping). Suggest adding a pre-roll gate: when canary changes weighted-fallback semantics, run a simulation that asserts fallback_weight does not increase when primary capacity reduces.

jordan: also recommend changing the canary autoscale script to require metric stability over a 3m window before increasing canary percentage above 10%. I'll open a PR for that.

ops-bot: checklist updated: owners set. Artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-incidents/RTE-2026-0423/.

sanjay: thanks everyone — I'll assemble the full RCA draft and post in #postmortems once artifacts are in. For now, fill the incident tracker: https://internal.redwood/incidents/RTE-2026-0423 (add timeline + owners).

katie: one last note — there were a few customer retry storms that made the dev-tier pressure worse. We'll add a short-term mitigation: exponential backoff enforcement at the gateway level for customers exceeding a burst threshold. Follow-up item in RCA. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (monitoring window stable). Please continue artifact collection for postmortem.

ash: assigning follow-ups to folks now. I'll draft the policy test and link it in the RCA.

maria: I have the customer impact matrix ready and will coordinate post-incident comms.

jordan: thanks team — great quick rollback and clear mitigation.

sanjay: end of thread — closing but keep pinging here for any late traces that surface.
